---
title: "ggpclient"
subtitle: "Download, label and consolidate data from the GGP data portal, in R"
toc: false
---

**ggpclient** is an R package for the [GGP data portal](https://www.ggp-i.org) of the Generations and Gender
Programme. It turns the portal's country-by-country downloads into analysis-ready data. It is the native R version of
the Python package [ggp-client](https://jossl95.github.io/ggp_client/): the same steps, the same folders, the same files
(see the [contract](contract.qmd)).

1. **Index** every dataset on the portal into a local catalogue: GGS rounds 1 and 2, the Family and Fertility Surveys
   (FFS), the Harmonized Histories and the Additional Datasets (the last two are only visible after login).
2. **Download** the files you select, by project, round, wave and country, and unpack zip and 7z archives.
3. **Preprocess** each data file (`.dta`, `.sav`, `.rds`, `.csv`, or FFS fixed-width `.dat` with its SPSS syntax) to
   parquet, with its variable and value labels in a `meta.json` file.
4. **Consolidate** the countries of each round and wave into one dataset, with one harmonized set of labels, as
   parquet and as a labelled Stata file.

```r
library(ggpclient)

p <- ggp_client(project = "ggs", round = 2)   # data_dir defaults to "data"

p |> ggp_login()                              # paste the access link (hidden)
p |> ggp_sync()
p |> ggp_download(ext = "dta")                # download: 25 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed
p |> ggp_preprocess()
p |> ggp_consolidate()                        # data/download/consolidated/ggs-ii_w1.parquet, ...
```

## Why

The portal ships every country as a separate archive, in several formats and with labels that differ between
countries. Working with all countries of a wave means downloading dozens of files by hand, reading Stata or SPSS files,
and stacking them while keeping track of which labels apply. ggpclient does that once, reproducibly, and keeps
everything it did in a log.

## Built with

[httr2](https://httr2.r-lib.org) for the downloads, [haven](https://haven.tidyverse.org) for Stata and SPSS files and
their labels, [arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/) and [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org) for parquet and for stacking
the countries, [archive](https://archive.r-lib.org) for zip and 7z, and [mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org) for the
background processes.
